question: A store offers two successive discounts on a product: the first is 12%, and the second is 8%. What is the single equivalent discount percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two successive discounts of x% and y%, use the net discount formula.

Net Discount % = x + y − (x × y ÷ 100)

Net Discount % = 12 + 8 − (12 × 8 ÷ 100)

Net Discount % = 20 − 0.96 = 19.04%

**∴ Answer = 19.04%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First discount (D₁) = 12%

Second discount (D₂) = 8%

**Formula used:**

Single Equivalent Discount = 1 − [(1 − d₁/100) × (1 − d₂/100)]
